q-28309.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14262816/assets/0ea627b0f4b68b4cde9c6ae07ceafcba35007556202ff5bf9a7981dee0ce5a7a.png)

Given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A)=\frac{12}{5},$ calculate the area (in square units) of $△ABC$ shown above.
q-28309.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC.
$$

We are given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A)=\frac{12}{5}.$ Notice that relative to $∠A,$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overset{―}{BC}$ and adjacent side $\overset{―}{AC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A) & =\frac{BC}{AC} \\ \frac{12}{5} & =\frac{10x+4}{6x-2} \\ 12(6x-2) & =5(10x+4) \\ 72x-24 & =50x+20 \\ 22x & =44 \\ x & =2\end{aligned}
$$

So, the side lengths are

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =10x+4=10(2)+4=24, \\ AC & =6x-2=6(2)-2=10.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 10\cdot 24 \\  & =120.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Given that tan⁡(m∠A)=125, calculate the area (in square units) of △ABC shown above.

a
100
b
120
c
160
d
140
e
90
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

In this case, the area of the right triangle is A=12AC⋅BC.

We are given that tan⁡(m∠A)=125. Notice that relative to ∠A, we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side BC― and adjacent side AC―. Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for x: tan⁡(m∠A)=BCAC125=10x+46x−212(6x−2)=5(10x+4)72x−24=50x+2022x=44x=2

So, the side lengths are

BC=10x+4=10(2)+4=24,AC=6x−2=6(2)−2=10.

Therefore, the area of △ABC is A=12AC⋅BC=12⋅10⋅24=120.

q-124471.name: Question 2
q-124471.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14262816/assets/f0d4e8ddf3a1b6cacab75f3207575695de5790f8223e30bc948e93daf37c939f.png)

In square units rounded to one decimal place, find the area of $△ABC$ shown above.
q-124471.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}BC\cdot AB.
$$

We are given that $m∠A={30}^{∘}.$ Notice that relative to $∠A,$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overset{―}{BC}$ and adjacent side $\overset{―}{AB}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A) & =\frac{BC}{AB} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡({30}^{∘}) & =\frac{x-1}{x+2} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡({30}^{∘})(x+2) & =x-1 \\ x\operatorname{tan}⁡({30}^{∘})+2\operatorname{tan}⁡({30}^{∘}) & =x-1 \\ x\operatorname{tan}⁡({30}^{∘})-x & =-1-2\operatorname{tan}⁡({30}^{∘}) \\ x(\operatorname{tan}⁡({30}^{∘})-1) & =-1-2\operatorname{tan}⁡({30}^{∘}) \\ x(1-\operatorname{tan}⁡({30}^{∘})) & =1+2\operatorname{tan}⁡({30}^{∘}) \\ x & =\frac{1+2\operatorname{tan}⁡({30}^{∘})}{1-\operatorname{tan}⁡({30}^{∘})} \\ x & =5.098\,0…\end{aligned}
$$

So, the side lengths are 

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =x-1=5.098\,0-1=4.098\,0…, \\ AB & =x+2=5.098\,0+2=7.098\,0….\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}(4.098\,0…)(7.098\,0…) \\  & =14.543\,8… \\  & ≈14.5,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the one decimal place.

EXPLANATION

In this case, the area of the right triangle is A=12BC⋅AB.

We are given that m∠A=30∘. Notice that relative to ∠A, we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side BC― and adjacent side AB―. Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for x:

tan⁡(m∠A)=BCABtan⁡(30∘)=x−1x+2tan⁡(30∘)(x+2)=x−1xtan⁡(30∘)+2tan⁡(30∘)=x−1xtan⁡(30∘)−x=−1−2tan⁡(30∘)x(tan⁡(30∘)−1)=−1−2tan⁡(30∘)x(1−tan⁡(30∘))=1+2tan⁡(30∘)x=1+2tan⁡(30∘)1−tan⁡(30∘)x=5.0980…

So, the side lengths are BC=x−1=5.0980−1=4.0980…,AB=x+2=5.0980+2=7.0980….

Therefore, the area of △ABC is

A=12(4.0980…)(7.0980…)=14.5438…≈14.5, rounded to the one decimal place.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14262816/assets/6d32c4a97154570f8a66f89ba5fee46f11aa09d2cd152edb4aa05f2613d035f3.png)

Given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠B)=\frac{3}{2},$ the **exact** area of $△ABC$ shown above is{{field-1}} square units.
q-244471.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC.
$$

We are given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠B)=\frac{3}{2}.$ Notice that relative to $∠B,$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overset{―}{AC}$ and adjacent side $\overset{―}{BC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠B) & =\frac{AC}{BC} \\ \frac{3}{2} & =\frac{x+3}{3x-5} \\ 3(3x-5) & =2(x+3) \\ 9x-15 & =2x+6 \\ 7x & =21 \\ x & =3\end{aligned}
$$

So, the side lengths are

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =3x-5=3(3)-5=4, \\ AC & =x+3=3+3=6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 6\cdot 4 \\  & =12.\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14262816/assets/58af9726d81e1d926f814736fa92dc95c427d4346c40252470380f51a5fcf50a.png)

Given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =3,$ the **exact** area of $△ABC$ shown above is{{field-1}} square units.
q-251125.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC.
$$

We are given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =3,$ where $\theta =m∠B.$ Notice we're also given the length of the side $\overset{―}{AC}$ opposite to $∠B.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to find the length of the adjacent side $\overset{―}{BC}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta  & =\frac{AC}{BC} \\ 3 & =\frac{15}{BC} \\ BC & =\frac{15}{3} \\ BC & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 15\cdot 5 \\  & =37.5.\end{aligned}
$$
